Subject: Quick Q on SLAB vs burst pilots for Optimize toolkit

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked promising. Before we put together an internal ask I wanted to clarify a couple things around how you recommend structuring a pilot for a series-B logistics app like ours. Two quick questions: 1) For a bursty workload (end-of-day routing spikes) should we aim for a slab (reserved) commit with burst credits or run purely on burst/hosted usage during the pilot? 2) Any recommendations on quantization levels you suggest for the 8B models to balance cost vs SLOs?

Rough context: BrightRoute processes ~80k route-generation requests/day but 70% of those happen in 3 short windows. Our SLO is p95 generation under 550ms. We'd like a 6–8 week pilot that lets us validate real-world cost curves and tail latencies.

Appreciate any practical framing you can share — if useful I can send a sample traffic trace.

Best,
Theo
Head of Platform
BrightRoute

P.S. we prefer credits over big upfront invoices during pilot phase.

Subject: RE: Quick Q on SLAB vs burst pilots for Optimize toolkit

Theo — great questions, thanks for the usage color. Short answer: pilot = hybrid slab baseline + burst cushion. Longer: see bullets + attached term sheet.

Key recommendations:
- Pilot structure: 8-week hybrid pilot. Reserve a modest slab sized at ~40% of your 95th percentile baseline to guarantee capacity for steady-state smoothing. Provide a burst credit pool (tokens) sized to accommodate your historical peak windows (we can size this after you share traces).
- Why hybrid: Slab reduces cold-start and ensures steady throughput at predictable unit-cost. Burst credits let you absorb cost of short peaks without an expensive reserve. For conversion offers we typically map slab commits to a graduated discount schedule.
- Credit mechanics: We can issue $7,500 in pilot credits that apply to burst usage only; slab consumption billed against the demo rate (discounted). If you convert within 30 days of pilot end, we can apply up to $5k of the pilot credits toward first quarter committed spend.
- Quantization guardrails (8B family): start with FP16 or dynamic int8 for generator models to keep tail-latency within SLO; int4 is attractive for cost but increases variance — recommend A/B runs during pilot (int8 vs int4 with KV-cache warmups). For your p95 <550ms target, int8 with KV-prefetching and adaptive batching is the safe default.
- Ops/Perf knobs: enable prefix/KV caching for frequent route templates, configure adaptive batching to keep 80–90ms per-token execution but small batch sizes during spikes. We can ship an instrumentation dashboard to measure hit rates and effective tokens per request.

Attachments: BR_pilot_term_sheet_optimize_toolkit.pdf (term sheet + credit mechanics) and latency_vs_cost_modeling_May2027.xlsx (starter model you can drop your trace into).

Next steps:
1) If that structure works, share one week's anonymized traces and we size the burst pool.
2) We'll send a short MSA addendum for pilot credits and an ops checklist for KV cache integration.

I'll loop Rishi on discount bands and Camila on pilot integration.

Thanks,
Olga

Proposed conversion discount ladder (draft):
- Commit >= $25k/mo slab for 12 months -> 22% discount on token rates + 6-month price protection
- Commit >= $10k/mo slab for 12 months -> 15% discount + 3-month price protection

Olga — I like the hybrid pilot. A couple of notes on the ladder: the 22% at $25k/mo is tight but workable if we cap burst credit exposure and require a quarterly usage review tied to autoscale triggers. Suggest we:
- Add a cap on monthly burst consumption that scales with slab size (e.g., burst pool = 1.5x slab nominal throughput during pilot).
- Add a 30-60 day operational checkpoint clause where we review KV hit rate and tail latency; if hit rate <60% we reserve the right to recommend additional ops engineering prior to conversion.

On quantization: agree with int8 default. Add a metric gating rule: if int4 yields p95 variance >20% relative to FP16 baseline in A/B, we won't recommend conversion to int4 for production. We'll instrument sample traces during pilot to determine the break-even.

I'll draft a short attachment-free amendment to the term sheet with these guardrails.

Rishi
